name: Ethics and Responsibility
description:
In everyday life, people act in different social roles – for example as students, team members, leaders, citizens, or consumers. In these roles, they make decisions and assume responsibility, both individually and as members of communities.
Such decisions are often guided by moral intuitions, personal convictions, or socially established values. But where do these convictions come from? How can decisions be made responsibly when others bear the consequences of our actions? And how should we deal with conflicts of interest in which different positions appear equally justified?
Ethics provides concepts and methods for systematically reflecting on such decision-making situations. It enables us to critically analyze moral conflicts and to develop reasoned judgments that go beyond individual intuitions.
